candidates.attacker_control: The attacker controls the HTTP parameter 'changenote' posted to Edit.jsp (WikiContext.EDIT). Edit.jsp also copies it unescaped into the session (line 247) and into the editor/preview templates, giving an additional reflected variant on the editor pages (templates/*/editors/plain.jsp value="${changenote}", templates/*/editors/preview.jsp hidden field).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that JSPWiki's markup parser escapes page text (m_rawHTML default false) - not relevant here because the value is a page attribute, not page content. Checked other renderers of the same attribute: MessageTag, AuthorTag, and RecentChangesPlugin escape or use JDOM text nodes (RecentChangesPlugin line 200-202 is escaped by JDOM serialization), and Comment.jsp (line 86) and AttachmentServlet (lines 516-522) escape this exact field - so the omission in Edit.jsp/default templates is inconsistent with project policy rather than intended. Confirmed SpamFilter/DefaultFilterManager do not normalize page attributes on save, and WikiPage.setAttribute stores the value as-is. Confirmed both shipped templates are affected and the sink is outside any wiki:Permission block (only view permission is required of the victim).
candidates.impact: Stored XSS in the wiki origin. The payload is persistent (page metadata) and executes for any viewer of the page's Info tab, including administrators; it enables session/cookie theft (JSPWiki sessions, assertion/cookie-auth cookies), CSRF-style privileged actions, and self-propagating wiki defacement. candidates.prerequisites: Attacker has an account with 'edit' permission on at least one page (the default JSPWiki policy grants editing at least to authenticated users; README describes the default wiki as freely editable). Victim only needs 'view' permission on that page and to open its Info tab (PageCommand.INFO requires only PageViewPermission, PageCommand.java line 57). No non-default configuration is needed: FileSystemProvider and the 'default' template are the shipped defaults.
candidates.root_cause: The change-note submitted with an edit is used without any HTML encoding along the whole path, while the same field is escaped in other code paths. Edit.jsp reads the raw parameter (line 73) and stores it on the page object (lines 167-170: modifiedPage.setAttribute(WikiPage.CHANGENOTE, changenote)); SaveWikiPageTask/FileSystemProvider persist it verbatim (FileSystemProvider.java lines 87-90 store, 136-140 load). The value is then written into the page-info history table without escaping: templates/default/InfoContent.jsp line 207 emits EL ${changenote} (EL performs no auto-escaping) and templates/210/InfoContent.jsp lines 247-249 emit <%= changenote %>. The mismatched escaping elsewhere (Comment.jsp line 86 escapes 'changenote'; AttachmentServlet.java lines 516-522 escapes the attachment change note) shows escaping was the intended handling and was simply omitted for the page-edit path.

candidates.unverified: No runtime reproduction was performed (read-only review); exploitability assumes a browser treats the page-info HTML output as markup, which follows directly from the JSP/EL source but was not executed. The exact default policy grant that lets a user edit (jspwiki.policy is not present in the snapshot) was inferred, so the attacker-prerequisite set may be narrower/wider in a given installation. It is also possible that the dataset's expected defect for this snapshot is a sibling unescaped sink (e.g. Captcha.jsp 'page' or InfoContent 'renameto'); those are documented as rejected leads.

coverage_summary: Coverage: 1155 model-visible source files (no binary/symlink/sensitive-name exclusions reported; all source text <=5 MiB). Inspected the security-relevant Java of jspwiki-main (auth/login/cookie modules, authorization and permission classes, WikiContext/WikiEngine/WikiSession, servlets: Attachment, Wiki, Ajax dispatcher, RPC/Atom, admin/user beans, providers, parser/rendering, filters, preferences, workflow) and jspwiki-util (Serializer, TextUtil, HttpUtil), plus the jspwiki-war JSPs and both template families (default and 210), web.xml, jspwiki.properties, poms and module configs. Searches covered escaping/sanitization helpers, request-parameter sinks, SQL, deserialization, XML parsing, path handling and file operations. Not exhaustively line-reviewed: every plugin/tag class, the markdown module internals, static JS/CSS assets, translated resource bundles, and the wikipage text corpora. The snapshot contains no test sources and no jspwiki.policy, and no code was executed.
limitations: Read-only source review: no build, no runtime deployment, no browser execution; all exploitability statements are source-derived inferences.

The shipped jspwiki.policy is absent from the snapshot, so the exact default permission grants for 'edit' (attacker prerequisite) and 'view' (victim prerequisite) could not be verified in-tree; conventional default-policy behavior was assumed and may differ per installation.

Because several independent unescaped-output sinks exist in this snapshot (change note, Captcha 'page', Info 'renameto', workflow facts, preferences cookie), the identity of the single intended defect is uncertain; the submitted candidate was chosen on evidence strength and impact, not on confirmed ground-truth matching.
Large portions of the Java codebase and many JSP/plugin files were reviewed by targeted search rather than complete reading; additional undiscovered issues may exist outside the inspected paths.
No sibling-run, patch, CVE or ground-truth data was consulted, per the review constraints.

rejected_leads.lead: Reflected XSS in Captcha.jsp via the 'page' parameter (line 43 escapes with TextUtil.replaceEntities, which does not encode single quotes, while line 110 interpolates it into a single-quoted value attribute).
rejected_leads.reason: Real escaping gap and anonymously reachable, but the sink element is type="hidden" (not focusable), so a reliable payload needs an injected style/overlay and mouse interaction; weaker evidence of practical exploitation than the stored change-note XSS.

rejected_leads.lead: Reflected XSS in templates/default/InfoContent.jsp and templates/210/InfoContent.jsp via the 'renameto' parameter (lines 42-43/44-45 read it raw; line 126/146 interpolate it unescaped into a double-quoted value attribute).
rejected_leads.reason: Genuine unescaped sink, but the form is wrapped in wiki:Permission permission="rename", so the victim must hold rename permission, and exploitation requires the victim to open a crafted link; weaker than a stored sink reachable with view-only permission.

rejected_leads.lead: Path traversal via the JSPWikiUID cookie in CookieAuthenticationLoginModule.getCookieFile (raw cookie -> new File(cookieDir, uid); clearLoginCookie -> cf.delete(), reachable from Logout.jsp; login() reads the file and uses its contents as a login principal).
rejected_leads.reason: Code weakness is real, but practical impact requires guessing absolute paths writable by the servlet user, cookie authentication is disabled by default (jspwiki.cookieAuthentication=false), and the file content is only used as a principal name, not disclosed; impact is less concrete than the stored XSS.

rejected_leads.lead: AtomAPIServlet.doPost saves pages without any authentication check ('FIXME: Do authentication here', line 127) via m_engine.saveText().
rejected_leads.reason: The /atom/* servlet mapping is commented out ('REMOVE ME TO ENABLE') in the shipped web.xml, so it is not reachable in the default configuration.

rejected_leads.lead: templates/default/WorkflowContent.jsp renders workflow fact values with c:out escapeXml="false" (line 104), which can hold page/diff text.
rejected_leads.reason: Requires an approver to be configured so that page-save approval workflows exist; not enabled by default, so reachability is configuration-dependent.

rejected_leads.lead: Preferences.parseJSONPreferences copies values from the JSPWikiUserPrefs cookie into session preferences without encoding (lines 134-149), and templates echo them via EL.
rejected_leads.reason: The data source is the victim's own cookie (attacker cannot set cookies for the wiki origin), making this self-XSS unless chained with another injection - not a standalone finding.

rejected_leads.lead: ShortURLConstructor.getForwardPage returns request parameter 'do' + '.jsp' used in WikiServlet's RequestDispatcher.forward (WikiServlet.java lines 96-100).
rejected_leads.reason: Only reachable when the non-default ShortURLConstructor is configured (default is DefaultURLConstructor, which returns a constant), and container path normalization limits traversal; unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: AttachmentServlet.validateNextPage only rejects values containing '://', allowing protocol-relative '//host' redirects (open redirect).
rejected_leads.reason: Requires a valid existing attachment the attacker may download; low security impact (CWE-601) compared to the stored XSS.

summary: Reviewed the JSPWiki 2.11.0.M3 snapshot (1155 files: jspwiki-main/java, jspwiki-util, jspwiki-markdown, jspwiki-war JSPs/templates/config, wikipages, portable/it-test configs). The strongest source-evidenced issue is a stored cross-site scripting flaw in the page change-note ("changenote") flow: the value taken from the edit form is persisted verbatim as a WikiPage attribute and later emitted with no HTML encoding in the page-info/history table of both shipped templates, executing in the browser of every user who opens the Info tab of the poisoned page. Other candidate sinks (Captcha.jsp single-quoted attribute, Info page "renameto" value attribute, cookie-auth path traversal, Atom API, workflow facts, preferences cookie) were examined but judged weaker or more configuration-dependent, and are listed as rejected/unconfirmed leads.
